headline: 2001 order on keeping the government neutral toward the labor relations of contractors on federal and federally funded construction projects.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order sets a policy that the federal government stays neutral toward how construction contractors handle their labor relations, such as their dealings with unions. It also aims to keep bidding open to competing contractors. It covers construction projects paid for by the federal government, fully or in part. No summary was provided, so the specific rules are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Construction contractors bidding on federal or federally funded projects
who_it_affects.how: The order addresses whether a contractor's labor arrangements can affect its ability to compete for this work.

who_it_affects.group: Construction workers and labor unions on these projects
who_it_affects.how: The order deals with how the government treats contractors' relationships with their workers and unions.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies and recipients of federal construction funds
who_it_affects.how: The order directs how they handle contractors' labor relations when awarding and managing construction projects.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed February 17, 2001; the title does not state a separate effective date.
